exact_prompt: Transparent six-view correction atlas, exactly 6 columns x 6 rows, view columns in order FRONT, TOP, RIGHT SIDE, LEFT SIDE, BOTTOM, REAR; rows exactly these six source objects: (1) snowy mountain peak; (2) long snowy mountain ridge; (3) straight snowy cliff wall; (4) L-shaped snowy cliff corner; (5) rocky snow slope mound; (6) low scree rubble patch. Use the source+current contact for exact source footprints, snowy stone palette and shape. All views are axis-aligned orthographic, no isometric camera. Front/rear/side elevations show only the correct vertical projected silhouette with fixed object orientation; TOP/BOTTOM look directly along vertical axis and show plan/underside footprints with vertical faces occluded. Row1 mountain peak TOP must show centered summit and radial ridge/snow cap footprint, not a triangular vertical face. Row2 ridge TOP must show a long connected mountain spine running left-right with the ordered summits and slopes in plan. Row3 straight cliff wall FRONT and REAR are broad straight vertical cliff faces (not V/corner); TOP is only narrow rock/snow cap strip, not vertical cliff plane. Row4 cliff corner keeps an L footprint in TOP/BOTTOM, with all four elevation views broad full-height joined cliff wall faces, consistent height and material, no triangular ramp or missing long arm. Row5 stone slope TOP is direct overhead rough snow/stone mound footprint with no upright peak faces. Row6 scree patch FRONT/REAR are low rubble edge elevations, with rock height comparable to other edge views; not broad overhead ground planes. Preserve other object's current source identities. Each cell complete, no clipping or neighbors, centered, transparent margin, consistent size with sibling approved views, retain Ink-and-Lanterns painted pixel style, no labels or borders.
